newsitem.title: USA: US CORPORATE BONDS - Tobacco debt up, markets slow.
newsitem.headline: US CORPORATE BONDS - Tobacco debt up, markets slow.

text.p: Activity in tobacco bonds grabbed the attention of the U.S. corporate bond markets on Thursday as investors took a breather from the recent marathon of new issues, market players said.
Bonds of tobacco companies such as RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp and Philip Morris & Cos Inc rose on news that the states and the tobacco industry were close to reaching a liabilty settlement.
Spreads on RJR Nabisco debt tightened 10-25 basis points while spreads on Philip Morris debt tightened five to eight basis points, traders said.
In the broader markets, high-yield bonds were unchanged to slightly lower as weakness in new issues pulled the prices of some bonds in the secondary market lower.
Traders said several recent new issues that were priced aggressively with low coupons were still under pressure.
Big Flower Press Inc $250 million in nine percent senior subordinated notes due '07 were bid at 98 1/4 on Thursday after being priced at 99.179 on Tuesday, traders said.
Outdoor Systems Inc $500 million in nine percent senior subordinated notes due '07 were heard at 98 3/4 today after pricing at 99.184, traders said.

In new-issue action on Thursday, Hayes Wheels International Inc sold $250 million in 10-year senior subordinated notes, rated B3/B, to yield 9.125 percent. CIBC Wood Gundy Securities Corp was the lead underwriter.
While the deal was increased from an original size of $200 million, it priced wide of price talk of nine percent.
The bonds, which were priced at par, were heard slightly weaker at 99 3/4-100 by the end of the day.
Later on Thursday, Oxford Automotive Inc sold $125 million in 10-year senior subordinated notes via Salomon Brothers Inc. The Caa1/B-minus bonds were priced to yield 10.125 percent.
The bonds, which were priced at 99.851, were quoted at 101 at the end of the day, lending credence to the view that junk bonds with higher coupons were in stronger demand, traders said.
In the investment-grade market, traders said prices of most high-grade bonds were firm amid slow trading activity, traders said.
New investment-grade bond issuance slowed from its torrid pace earlier in the week.
Today's deals included, Westvaco Corp's offering of $150 million in 30-year debentures, rated A1/A. The deal priced at 76 basis points over comparable Treasuries via Merrill Lynch & Co.
In the Treasury market, prices ended largely unchanged on Thursday, as a late bout of short-covering brought the market off lows that prevailed for most of the session.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury rose 3/32 to 99-9/32. Its yield dropped to 6.68 percent.
